units.text: In this video, you'll choose which service should verify temporary access to private content. For CloudFront, the application first authenticates the viewer and signs a U R L or cookie with its private key. The distribution verifies it against a public key in its trusted key group.

Use a signed U R L for a single object and signed cookies when access covers a set, such as video files. A valid request can hit the edge cache; for a miss, CloudFront can use Origin Access Control to fetch private S three content. Viewer access and origin permission are separate.

A CloudFront signed U R L points to the distribution and CloudFront verifies the viewer signature. An S three presigned U R L instead points directly to the S three operation, signed with credentials authorized for that action. The direct S three request does not use the CloudFront cache.

Choose CloudFront signing for controlled access through the distribution; choose S three presigning for a specific direct S three operation such as a temporary upload. Match the expiration and scope to the task. Origin Access Control is still a separate permission for CloudFront to fetch private S three objects.

In this video, you'll decide what CloudFront caches and how to avoid hiding a recovery behind stale cached responses. On a miss, an origin error can trigger a configured custom page and viewer status. In this example, an origin 500 is shown to the viewer as 503 with a custom page.

A cached error can outlive the origin outage. Inspect origin-side evidence as well as viewer status, and choose error caching duration to balance reduced repeated origin traffic against prompt recovery. Don't assume a friendly error page indicates an available backend.

Cache identity and forwarded values are different. In this example the path and language influence the cached variant; the session cookie can be forwarded without becoming part of the key. If an excluded value changes the resulting response, include a safe variant in the cache key or avoid caching that response.

Use T T L policy to control freshness. A positive minimum T T L can keep content cached even with restrictive origin cache headers. Use new versioned paths for immutable assets or invalidate a stable path when it really must change. A hit needs no origin fetch; a miss does.
